events.t: SUCW 2026 Kickoff!
events.d: Join us LIVE! from Beer Hall at Union Hall as we kick off festivities for the 10th Annual StartupCincy Week!

events.t: Food Founder Kickoff presented by Kroger
events.d: Before we dig in to the day, VP of Strategic Planning for Kroger, Stephanie Jenkins will kick off the Food Founder Track with a welcome to Cincinnati’s founders, foodies, makers, and industry leaders. Come hungry—for ideas, connections, and lots of food for thought.

events.t: Ohio’s #1 for Business. Now What?
events.d: Ohio is having a moment - but what will it take to keep the momentum going? JobsOhio CFO Andrew Deye and REDI Cincinnati CEO Kimm Lauterbach tackle the big bets, opportunities and priorities that will shape Cincinnati and Ohio’s next decade of growth.

events.t: Stop Building Audiences. Start Building Community.
events.d: Founders obsess over followers, impressions, and content calendars — and wonder why growth feels like shouting into the void. The problem isn't your strategy. It's your mental model. An audience is a crowd. A community is a competitive moat. Amy Vaughan has spent 15+ years building both — from enterprise campaigns for Ford and P&G to a national digital community of 500+ women to a physical coworking space designed around belonging, not square footage. She's here to show founders exactly where the audience-first playbook breaks down, and what to build instead.

events.t: Chef and Coffee Morning Happy Hour
events.d: Chef & Coffee is built to bring Cincinnati’s food and hospitality community together over conversation and connection. After a quick introduction to the community and what it offers, we’ll open the room for intentional networking, using guided prompts and icebreakers to spark meaningful new connections.

events.t: Gen Z Unfiltered: The Future of AI + Society
events.d: This candid fireside chat-style panel offers an inside look at perceptions, concerns, and behaviors around AI from emergent Gen-Z leaders in the University of Cincinnati's Foresight Lab. Grounded in structured futures research and an unfiltered generational perspective from lived experience, we’ll challenge assumptions, surface tensions, and debate what’s next for AI and society without the polished talking points.

events.t: Your Corner Of the Internet
events.d: Everyone should have their own personal website. A personal website can be a low stakes creative outlet, a powerful career building tool, or anything in between. Bring your laptop to this mini workshop where you'll buy a domain name and get started on a personal website—your corner of the internet. (Or just come observe and ask questions!)

events.t: Building Ecosystems in the Big Three: What Cincinnati, Cleveland, and Columbus Can Learn From One Another
events.d: Ohio’s three largest cities are each building thriving startup ecosystems—but they’re doing it in distinctly different ways. Leaders from Cincinnati, Cleveland, and Columbus compare notes on what’s working, what they can learn from one another, and how stronger connections across the Three C’s could accelerate Ohio’s innovation economy.

events.t: A Brand That Grows With You - Brand Strategy Workshop
events.d:
Small businesses often jump straight into logos, websites, and marketing without clarity on their brand—and it shows. This interactive workshop is designed to slow that process down just enough to build a stronger, more intentional foundation.

Rather than focusing on visuals or trends, this session guides participants through a hands-on brand strategy experience. Attendees will actively work through core brand-building exercises, including defining brand values, identifying a primary brand archetype, clarifying target audiences and personas, and aligning those insights into a clear strategic direction.

events.t: Start Small, Grow Slow: Life Before Brick and Mortar
events.d: Panel discussion on the impact of starting small as a small food business. Highlighting the importance of building a drive for your product, community buy-in, and sustainable growth. Additionally talking through the different ways in which businesses can start small.

events.t: Five Ingredients for Building the Future Economy Here
events.d:
The Great Lakes Super Region does not lack the raw ingredients for a generational technology economy. It has the population, universities, industrial customers, technical talent, research institutions, operating knowledge, and economic scale.

What it lacks is system behavior.

To reclaim its role as one of the world’s most important innovation economies, the region needs five things...

events.t: City as a Lab: From “What If?” to “What’s Next?”
events.d: What happens when a city becomes a testing ground for new ideas? Go inside Cincinnati’s City as a Lab initiative to hear what’s working, what we’re learning, and what still needs to change to make it easier for startups and cities to innovate together.

events.t: Out of Office: Fresh Perspectives
events.d: A guided walk-and-talk experience designed to offer a literal breath of fresh air. This session facilitates natural networking on the go, allowing founders and investors to fall into step and connect while moving through the outdoors. This session will meet at the Cincinnat Art Week HQ!

events.t: Building a Better Brainstorm: Lessons from Cincinnati’s Most Creative Minds
events.d: Creativity is often treated as a lightning strike moment, but the best ideas are usually the result of intentional environments, movement, curiosity and human connection. In this session, award-winning PR strategist Allison Brinkman Schroeder shares lessons gathered through immersive conversations and experiences with Cincinnati creatives across food, art, entertainment, business and beyond. Attendees will explore how experiential thinking, sensory input, and unconventional brainstorming techniques can unlock stronger collaboration and more innovative ideas. Participants will leave with practical, immediately applicable ways to build more engaging, effective and human-centered brainstorms.

events.t: Rooted & Real: How Small Business Owners Build Jobs, Careers and Community When Competing with Corporate
events.d: Exploring how independent business owners invest in their people and their neighborhoods in ways that large corporations simply can't — and how that becomes their greatest competitive advantage.

events.t: Personal Branding for the 99%
events.d: How founders and leaders can build a personal brand that helps them with their goals, without having to become a content creator.

events.t: Beltways Debuts America’s First Accelerator at First Financial Center
events.d: Join Beltways at First Financial Center for an invitation-only media event marking the public launch of America’s first accelerator: the world's smartest, safest, and fastest moving walkway. Invited guests will experience the technology firsthand, meet the team behind it, and have the opportunity to ride the M5 at full speed. Local and national media will be filming. Light refreshments will be provided. Capacity is limited to 50 guests and admission is by application only. (https://luma.com/nf6e83vn)

events.t: Community Lunch at Washington Park
events.d: Join us for lunch at Washington Park with a casual midday break full of fellow founders, funders, and entrepreneurship enthusiasts. Good food, great company, and one of OTR’s best gathering spots. Lunches are first come, first serve - so don't miss out!

events.t: The Consultant You Didn’t Think to Hire: Leveraging Fresh Perspectives and Community Resources with ESP461 Entrepreneurial Consulting
events.d: Through this conversation, attendees will gain insight into what to expect during a consulting engagement, how students tackle complex business challenges, and the measurable outcomes these collaborations can produce. Participants will leave with a better understanding of how to leverage university talent and community resources to support growth, innovation, and problem-solving within their own organizations.

events.t: Building a Movement Before You Build a Business
events.d: What makes people care enough to show up, come back, and bring others with them? In this energetic and interactive session, Allyson West shares lessons from building Cincinnati's independent film ecosystem and creating a community-driven brand that people proudly champion. Attendees will leave inspired and equipped with practical tools to turn audiences into advocates, customers into ambassadors, and ideas into movements.

events.t: Releasing Blocks to Action
events.d: This workshop invites participants to explore how innovation and meaningful action begin from within. Through experiential embodiment practices, attendees will identify internal barriers, connect with their felt sense, and discover new possibilities for creativity, courageous action, and sustainable growth.

events.t: Welcome To The Ecosystem @ StartupCincy Week
events.d: Wondering where to start? Meet the organizations, programs, and people powering our region’s startup community—all in one place. This StartupCincy fan favorite is your one-stop shop for discovering the resources, connections, and support available to help you take your next step.

events.t: Communicating Your Design Needs: How & When to Ask for Help
events.d: Good design isn't just about how something looks — it's about how it works, who it's for, and why it matters. This session shows small business owners and entrepreneurs how the same design thinking and consumer insight process that shapes great physical products can sharpen every aspect of their business. We'll explore how to identify what you actually need from a creative partner, how to communicate it clearly, and how to use AI tools wisely without letting them replace the human thinking that drives real innovation. Walk away with a new lens for solving problems — whether you're developing a product, a service, or a strategy.

events.t: From Strategy to Story: Building Your Company and Personal Narrative
events.d: Audience members will learn how to craft stories that move people to action -- making customers buy, investors back, and people believe in you. Topics include starting with stories—not slides; avoiding "buzzword bingo"; understanding what makes a compelling message, proof point, and story; and finding the intersection between what you want to say and what your audience wants to hear. Led by CincyTech Executive-in-Residence and communications advisor Bryan McCleary, the session will also cover how to command a room in high-stakes moments.

events.t: The 1-Hour Pitch Deck: AI Workflows to Turn Ideas Into Influence
events.d: AI has made it easier than ever to build a Pitch Deck, yet harder than ever to create one that stands out—and actually persuades—during high-stakes moments. In this tactical, fast-paced session, Rolando Archila will show founders and leaders the exact method that combines AI agents & workflows with timeless human-centered storytelling to turn messy ideas into clear, credible, high-stakes narratives. Attendees will learn the right way to use AI for persuasive storytelling: not to generate generic slides, but to sharpen thinking, surface proof, structure the story, and make ideas land with investors, customers, executives, and boardrooms. Whether raising capital, selling a bold vision, or winning executive buy-in, this session gives attendees a practical workflow for making their ideas hard to ignore.

events.t: The Cost of Avoidance: The Hidden Psychology Behind Business Money Decisions
events.d: Money decisions in business are rarely just about numbers. Fear, avoidance, scarcity, uncertainty, and even overconfidence quietly influence how entrepreneurs approach pricing, growth, hiring, cash flow, and taxes often without realizing it. Through candid discussion, real-world examples, and interactive reflection, attendees will explore the hidden psychology behind business money decisions and uncover the patterns that may be shaping their business choices.

events.t: Building a Show Like a Startup: The Making of Coworking
events.d: What does it take to build a television series the same way you build a startup? In this session, The Coworking crew and cast share how a Cincinnati-based team developed, funded, produced, and marketed an original comedy microseries inspired by startup culture and modern work life. Attendees will get a behind-the-scenes look at the rapidly growing world of microseries, vertical storytelling, and microdramas, and why these emerging formats are creating new opportunities for creators, brands, and entrepreneurs.

events.t: UC Tech Transfer: Recruiting Venture Builders, Connecting Startups, and Commercializing Innovation
events.d:
The University of Cincinnati's Tech Transfer & Commercialization Office at the 1819 Innovation Hub does more than file patents. It actively engages in the continued development and commercialization of university innovations across multiple pathways. One of those pathways is a founder-friendly model built specifically to match venture builders with UC technologies, inventors, and early-stage funding opportunities to co-create new Ohio companies. This session pulls back the curtain on how that process works, and what other commercialization and partnership options exist for existing startups and companies looking to leverage UC research and capabilities. Whether you're sourcing your next venture or looking to accelerate an existing one, UC's portfolio of innovations and partnership programs may be exactly what you've been missing.

Sponsored By University of Cincinnati

events.t: Latinos in Entrepreneurship
events.d: Hear from Latino founders and community leaders about the experiences, opportunities, and challenges shaping entrepreneurship today. This conversation will explore what it takes to build, grow, and create opportunity—and how we can strengthen pathways for the next generation of Latino entrepreneurs.

events.t: The Talent Engine Fueling Cincinnati’s Entrepreneurial Ecosystem
events.d:
What does it take to scale a startup when talent, time, and resources are limited?

Join this panel discussion on how Cincinnati founders are leveraging UC co-op talent to build teams, accelerate growth, and reach key business milestones. Learn how experiential learning creates value for both startups and students while strengthening the region's innovation ecosystem.

Whether you're a founder, hiring manager, or ecosystem builder, you'll leave with practical insights on developing a sustainable pipeline of emerging talent.

Sponsored by University of Cincinnati

events.t: Community by Design
events.d: How do you design belonging? Hear from an array of Cincinnati community builders as they explore how belonging is intentionally cretaed through creative experiences - from wine and art to hospitality and entrepreneurship. Discover what founders and ecosystem builders can learn from those experiences and connections that shape a thriving city.

events.t: Organizing the Story: How to Build A Narrative System for Startups and Small Businesses
events.d: Most founders have a story, but few have a system for telling it consistently across pitches, websites, social media, and investor conversations. In this hands-on session, you will learn a clear framework for organizing your story, then put it to work using AI prompts and your existing tech stack to build a narrative system that runs without you. You will walk out with the structure, tools, and prompts to keep your message sharp and consistent as your business grows.

events.t: Small Business, Big Insights: Turning Customer Understanding into Growth
events.d:
This engaging panel will explore how small businesses can turn customer understanding into smarter decisions, stronger relationships, and sustainable growth. Designed for entrepreneurs and startup founders, the session will highlight practical ways to use data, customer feedback, and consumer insights to better understand what customers want, how they behave, and what keeps them coming back. Panelists will share perspectives from retail data science and consumer insights, offering real-world examples and actionable guidance on how businesses of any size can listen more intentionally, identify growth opportunities, and make informed choices that support long-term success.

Sponsored by Sam Adams, Brewing the American Dream

events.t: Your Professor Wants More Than a Lab: How Universities Are Becoming Startup Engines
events.d: Universities are no longer just places for research and publications. They are increasingly becoming launchpads for startups, patents, venture funding, and real-world innovation. This session explores how professors, researchers, students, and commercialization leaders work together to transform academic discoveries into scalable companies and technologies. Attendees will gain an inside look at how academic entrepreneurship actually works, from intellectual property and tech transfer to startup formation, ecosystem building, and founder development.

events.t: Beyond Product-Market Fit: Why Co-Founder Fit Matters More Than You Think
events.d: Attendees will hear an honest, research-informed exploration of the hidden dynamics that shape co-founder relationships and ultimately impact company culture, growth, and resilience. Through real founder stories, practical frameworks, and reflection prompts, participants will learn how to recognize signs of misalignment, evaluate relationship fit, and navigate difficult partnership dynamics before they create lasting organizational damage. The session is designed to be both deeply relatable and immediately applicable for founders at any stage.

events.t: The Human Edge: Why Your Story Is Your Strongest Marketing Asset in an AI World
events.d: Every founder has access to the same AI tools, the same content templates, and the same generic marketing advice. So why do some businesses create instant connection while others disappear into the noise? The answer doesn’t come from a better prompt or a full content calendar. It comes from knowing your story, told with intention, to the right person at the right time in the right place. Led by the pioneers of Connection Marketing — an approach to business growth that prioritizes human storytelling as a catalyst for real relationships — this session teaches founders how to uncover the deeper narrative behind their business, helping to unlock stronger connection with their clients, colleagues, and community.

events.t: SPEED COACHING: Turning Customer Insights into Action: consumer insights, marketing, PR, selling skills and MORE!
events.d:
Following the Small Business, Big Insights panel, entrepreneurs are invited to join small group speed coaching designed to help translate customer understanding into practical business growth strategies. Coaches, local experts, and Boston Beer professionals will build on the panel discussion by helping business owners think through how to gather useful feedback, interpret customer behavior, identify opportunities, and apply insights to decisions around sales, marketing, product development, and customer experience. Speed coaching will be organized in three 25-minute rounds, giving entrepreneurs the flexibility to join a table, ask questions, and receive actionable guidance tailored to their business. Whether you are trying to better understand your current customers, reach new audiences, or make smarter growth decisions, this session will help you turn insights into next steps.

Sponsored By Sam Adams Brewing the American Dream

events.t: The Outlier Advantage: What Atypical Founders Get Right That the Room Keeps Missing
events.d: The startup ecosystem has a default founder profile. When you don't match it, you face a choice: perform the pattern or use the gap. This talk is about using the gap - and why the same profile that reads as an outlier in certain rooms is the exact profile that unlocks distribution networks, markets, and talent that pattern-matched founders may never reach.

events.t: Buried: Why Mission-Driven Founders Sound Generic — and How to Lead With Story Instead
events.d: Mission-driven founders and small business owners know their work matters — but somewhere between investor decks, customer demands, and daily operational pressure, the story that made them start the company gets buried. This session names why that happens to even the most purposeful operators, reframes story as a leadership function rather than a marketing deliverable, and runs a live exercise that pulls your real narrative back to the surface. You'll leave leading with the story that's actually yours – not the polished one you've been outsourcing.

events.t: Community Kickoff Happy Hour! presented by Sam Adams
events.d: Raise a glass to entrepreneurship as we kick off an exciting week of innovation, inspiration, and connection—powered by our friends at Sam Adams!

events.t: Cintrifuse Annual Meeting
events.d: A decade of investment in Cincinnati’s startup ecosystem is paying off—and setting the stage for what comes next. Cintrifuse CEO J.B. Kropp explores the founders, capital, talent, and momentum shaping Cincinnati’s next chapter, followed by a fireside chat with entrepreneur Jake Rouse on what it takes to build—and keep building—from Cincinnati.
events.c: Free add-on to any StartupCincy Week ticket (0.00 on the registration form)

events.t: Entrepreneurship in Franchising
events.d: From starting a brick and mortar side hustle to 75+ location franchisor - a new take on franchising and discussion on franchising as an alternative 'ETA' strategy.

events.t: Mapping Technology from Idea to Market
events.d: While moving from a proof of concept to a physical, market-ready prototype is a major milestone, many brilliant hardtech founders stall out before their technology ever hits the real world. In this session, Torrey Babson of BRITE Energy Innovators outlines a practical roadmap to help early-stage startups securely cross this pre-commercialization valley. Drawing on real-world challenges faced within the Silicon Heartland, he will break down how founders can leverage structured accelerator pathways and fractional executive talent to fortify operations for fundraising success.

events.t: Beyond the SAFE
events.d: Most founders default to a SAFE for early financing because it's what they've seen. But the instrument you choose shapes your company's trajectory, your ownership, and your life as a founder — often more than the valuation does. This session brings together practitioners behind three distinct structures to walk through how each works, when it performs best, and what it actually looks like in the docs.

events.t: Two Cities, One Startup: Building & Backing Kernel
events.d: Kernel cofounder Catherine Jue and Accel’s Daniel Levine join Cintrifuse Capital’s Max Dworin for a candid look at the founder and investor journey. Through Kernel’s experience building simultaneously in Cincinnati and San Francisco, they’ll explore raising institutional capital, navigating founder-investor relationships, and what it means to build an ambitious startup across two very different innovation ecosystems.

events.t: Buying a Business: The Path to Entrepreneurship with a Huge Headstart
events.d: Most entrepreneurs think they have two choices: get a job or start a business. There's a third path—buying a company with customers, employees, and cash flow already in place. This session will explore how business acquisition works, who it's right for, and how aspiring entrepreneurs can use it to accelerate their path to ownership.

events.t: Founder Financial Discipline: Make Better Decisions with Limited Capital
events.d:
Every startup operates with limited capital, but many founders make spending, hiring, and growth decisions without clear visibility into burn rate, runway, or financial tradeoffs. This practical, interactive workshop helps founders understand how their decisions affect available capital and gives them a simple framework for improving financial discipline.

Rather than focusing on accounting theory, the session is built around real founder decisions: what to spend, when to hire, how to evaluate growth investments, and how to create a monthly rhythm for reviewing financial health. Attendees will leave with clear, actionable tools they can use immediately to make better decisions with the capital they already have.

events.t: Connecting the Conversation: Main Street to VC
events.d: SMBs have surfaced as one of the 'final frontiers' for technology, especially for AI-native startups, but building and growing a startup that serves owners & operators on Main Street is a fundamentally different mode than enterprise SaaS. This session will be a conversation between a Main Street owner-operator, a startup founder, and an investor actively investing in SMB tech, so we can see where the most meaningful connections are happening, what gets lost in translation, and how SMB operators are experiencing this new wave of technology.

events.t: Build your first AI agent, no technical skills required
events.d:
AI is moving quickly, but for many teams, it still feels abstract. Notion AI Labs is a hands-on workshop designed to turn AI ideas into workflows your team can actually use.

Join us for a guided workshop where you’ll learn how agents work and how to connect them to the workflows already happening in your workspace. You’ll walk away with an agent that you can immediately put to work. No Notion experience or technical skills required.

Sponsored by Notion

events.t: Top 5 HR Mistakes Startups Make (and How to Fix Them)
events.d:
Book+Street is back, this time talking startup HR and how to get it right from the start. Startups are hard. We get it. When you’re moving fast, hiring fast, and figuring things out as you go, HR can get messy quickly. This session breaks down the people mistakes we see startups make most often, and how to fix them before they turn into bigger, more expensive problems.

We’ll cover hiring, compensation, team structure, and the HR basics founders need to think about early. The goal is simple: make smarter people decisions, avoid costly mistakes, and build a team that can grow with the business.

Sponsored by Book + Street

events.t: Put Down the Slop Cannon: How I Design and Build for Quality with AI
events.d: When anyone can ship, where's the edge now? It flows to what's scarce: knowing what to build, how it should feel, and whether it's any good. Nick Cramer is a product designer and former venture-backed founder who embeds with startups to shape, design, and build with agent-native tools every day. In this session he'll take a real app he's building and work on it live, showing the moves he uses to ship fast without shipping slop.

events.t: Building in Cincinnati: What Works, What Doesn’t, and What’s Next
events.d: Cincinnati has a lot going for it as a place to build a startup: deep industry expertise, a strong corporate base, a connected startup community, and a culture of capital efficiency. But we also have real gaps in areas like talent, capital, and startup density. This panel will bring together local founders and investors for a candid conversation about what Cincinnati does well, where we fall short, and where we should invest to make our ecosystem stronger.

events.t: Adding New Friends - Understanding Equity Awards for Co-founders, Employees, and Advisors
events.d:
Explaining how equity issuances to co-founders, early employees and service providers and advisors works, as well as some tangible data-driven advice about what the market standard is for how that happens, including an explanation of different vehicles (RSA's, Stock Options, etc.)

Sponsored by FBT Gibbons

events.t: Responsible AI: Simple Steps for Privacy, Security, and Governance Actionable Best Practices for Startups
events.d: In this practical panel, participants will discover easy-to-adopt strategies for AI governance, privacy, and security tailored specifically for startups with limited resources. Industry experts will provide clear, easy to implement guidance and real-world examples to help founders ensure compliance and build trustworthy, marketable AI products.

events.t: How AI Has Changed The Way We Speak to Our Customers
events.d: AI has rewired what marketers thought they understood: how customers experience their inbox, how marketing teams build and send campaigns, what "personalization at scale" actually means in practice, and more. This session highlights what has changed, how real marketing teams have adapted in real-time, and what's next.

events.t: How Fractional Leadership Accelerates Startup Commercialization Success
events.d: Early-stage ventures often face a critical bottleneck that capital alone cannot solve: a profound gap in execution-focused leadership talent. While traditional recruitment models are cost-prohibitive for pre-scale companies, the strategic deployment of embedded fractional talent offers an elegant solution for founders and investors alike. This session explores how placing seasoned operators directly inside early-stage operations lowers investor risk, optimizes cash burn, and shortens the timeline to commercial scale.

events.t: How Hypergrowth Leaders are Rethinking Talent in the Age of AI
events.d: The conversation will center on how hypergrowth companies are actively rethinking talent, organizational structure and the way teams operate in the age of AI. The goal is to make this very practical: what each of the panelists is seeing inside their organizations, what they are experimenting with, how roles or teams are changing, and what they think leaders should be preparing for over the next few years. The conversation will consist of experiences across engineering, product/operations and GTM to give the audience a range of perspectives.

events.t: 90 Days to Industry Fluency
events.d: Understanding that industry fluency is very different than industry expertise. Understanding that people don't question your knowledge if you use the right words. Understanding that founders often only need industry fluency

events.t: The Unicorn, Asteroid and Phoenix: The 80 Acres Story
events.d:
Entrepreneur Mike Zelkind left a successful career as a food industry executive to launch what would become one of Cincinnati’s first unicorns—80 Acres Farms. In his first public appearance since 80 Acres ceased operations, CEO and co-founder Mike Zelkind will tell the inside story of an extraordinary entrepreneurial journey—from launching the startup with co-founder Tisha Livingston at Union Hall, to building a Cincinnati unicorn that became a global leader during the explosive rise of vertical farming, to ultimately confronting the decision every founder hopes never to face.

Sponsored by CincyTech

events.t: Building a Smarter Startup: R&D Tax Credits and Tax Strategies That Fuel Growth
events.d:
Think tax strategy is just a year-end headache? For startups, it can be a growth engine. Join Forvis Mazars' Rob Summerford and Ryan Vaughan, with Brian Duerring, COO of Pantomath, for a practical look at how the R&D tax credit can offset payroll taxes and extend your runway—plus the state, local, and structuring considerations every founder should have on their radar. Real strategies, real founder perspective, no jargon

Sponsored by Forvis Mazars

events.t: Stop Rewarding Your Best People With More Work: How the Competence Tax Quietly Burns Out High Performers and What Founders Can Do Instead
events.d: Your highest performers are often your greatest asset, but they can also become your biggest organizational risk. This session introduces the Competence Tax, a leadership pattern that quietly leads to burnout, stalled team growth, and over dependence on a few key people. Attendees will leave with practical tools to build a more resilient team, protect their best people, and create an organization that can scale sustainably.

events.t: Cincy Does Demos: Best of Demo Night LIVE! at SUCW
events.d: Cintrifuse’s Best of Demo Night is back! Once a year, we spotlight the most exciting innovators from our monthly demo nights. From AI to Aerotech—and everything in between—experience live presentations from the region’s top startups as they showcase cutting-edge ideas, breakthrough technologies, and the next big opportunities in entrepreneurship. Don’t miss this chance to see innovation in action and connect with the tech leaders shaping Cincinnati’s startup ecosystem.

events.t: AI & IP: What You Own, What You Don't, and What Could Blow Up in Your Face
events.d:
You'll learn what's actually patentable in the AI era — including why the tide has shifted on software patents and what that means for your competitive moat. We'll cover the current state of AI-generated content and why, under today's law, your AI's output may not be protectable IP - and how to structure your workflows to capture ownership where you still can. You'll understand the serious risks of what your team feeds into LLMs, from trade secrets to customer data, and what happens to that information once it's in the model. And you'll leave with a practical framework to maximize what you can protect, avoid the legal landmines that are already catching companies off guard, and make smart IP decisions without wasting money on protections that won't hold up.

Sponsored by FBT Gibbons

events.t: The Big Bet Happy Hour! presented by Hard Rock Casino
events.d: Go all in at The Big Bet Happy Hour, presented by Hard Rock Casino, and celebrate StartupCincy Week with high-energy networking, bold ideas, and plenty of winning conversations.

events.t: Wednesday Welcome!
events.d: Start StartupCincy Week with a quick dose of inspiration from one of Cincinnati’s small business leaders. We’ll set the tone for the week with a celebration of entrepreneurship, community, and the people who bring big ideas to life every day.

events.t: The State of Ohio Hard Tech + Investing in Hard Tech
events.d: Software had its run, but the next decade of venture capital and industrial dominance belongs to physical innovation. In this 2026 State of the Union address, we map out the massive acceleration of hard tech and hardware investment across the Buckeye State. From high-stakes re-shoring initiatives to major aerospace and manufacturing deals, Ohio is uniquely positioned to lead the nation. We will unpack the macro funding trends driving the state forward, drill down into Cincinnati’s explosive physical AI and robotics ecosystem—anchored by hubs like the 1819 Innovation District—and set the pace for where capital, talent, and hardware infrastructure are moving next.

events.t: Pop-Up to Permanent: Rethinking the Path to Brick-and-Mortar
events.d: What if developers acted more like accelerators for small businesses? Using Race Street Collective and other Cincinnati experiments as a case study, this interactive session explores new approaches to storefront entrepreneurship—from smaller spaces and shorter leases to mentorship and shared resources—and invites attendees to help design a better on-ramp from pop-up to permanent.

events.t: Impact Investing in Action: Building Economic & Social Opportunity in the Midwest
events.d: Impact investing is reshaping how capital can drive both financial returns and meaningful change. This interactive workshop will break down the fundamentals, bust common myths, explore why the Midwest is uniquely positioned for impact-driven growth, and offer actionable ways for founders, investors, and community leaders to get involved.

events.t: Ten Year Vision, Day One Plan
events.d:
Anything's possible. But good things take time and most of us are either too afraid to start, or three years in and already exhausted trying to look like a company we haven't actually built yet.

In this 30-minute session, Rachel Desrochers digs into the honest gap between where you are and where you're pretending to be — whether that's Day One or Year Three, and what it actually takes to stop worrying about tomorrow long enough to act today.

You'll leave with one clear, honest next step, sized for right now instead of the version of you that hasn't arrived yet.

Sponsored by The Gratitude Collective

events.t: The Factory Floor Robotics Evolution
events.d: Robotic arms have been the backbone of manufacturing for decades, but deploying them in modern, agile factory environments still presents massive integration, software, and safety challenges. At the same time, the hardware world is flooded with hype surrounding humanoid robots, leaving many to wonder if traditional articulated arms are on the verge of extinction. This session cuts through the noise to examine the true state of manufacturing robotics. We will break down the immediate technical hurdles of deploying next-generation arms, explore new sensing and AI technologies keeping them relevant, and debate whether the future belongs to specialized, highly efficient arms or flexible, human-shaped machines.

events.t: What's Your Number? The Skill Nobody Teaches You and the One that Changes Everything
events.d: Attendees will hear Jackie Reau say plainly that she loves asking for money! Most people in the audience have likely never heard a successful founder say that out loud. They will work through a live exercise, writing down their actual number, not a range, before they leave the room, so the session produces a concrete deliverable rather than inspiration that fades by the next day.

events.t: The $5,000 Leap: How Small-Dollar “Leapfrog Capital” Can Unlock Your Next Stage of Growth
events.d:
In this workshop, we’ll discuss how a small cash injection can help take your business to the next level.

Takeaways:

How to identify whether a small cash injection could meaningfully accelerate your business

How to connect an investment in your business to increased revenue and growth

What makes a business a strong candidate for small-dollar growth capital

events.t: Out of Office: Fresh Perspectives
events.d: A guided walk-and-talk experience designed to offer a literal breath of fresh air. This session facilitates natural networking on the go, allowing founders and investors to fall into step and connect while moving through the outdoors. This session will meet at the Cincinnat Art Week HQ!

events.t: The Lonely Founder: Building Connection, Community, and Emotional Safety While You Build Your Business
events.d: Entrepreneurship is one of the most courageous things a person can do and one of the loneliest. In this workshop, Courtney Carroll, LPCC-S, licensed therapist and founder of Called 2 Encourage Counseling, guides founders through an honest conversation about the emotional weight of building something from nothing. Through reflection, somatic tools, and community connection, attendees will leave with language for what they've been carrying and practical strategies to stop carrying it alone.

events.t: Unlocking Technology Transfer Powerhouses
events.d: University tech transfer offices and military labs sit on a goldmine of uncommercialized innovation, yet they remain widely misunderstood and underutilized by hardware startups. Most founders view tech transfer as a single-shot transaction—acquiring an isolated piece of IP only if they happen to graduate from that specific institution. This session flips the script, mapping out how to proactively approach research hubs and build a comprehensive tech-licensing package. We will demystify the licensing pipeline, explore how to combine multiple technologies to create a moat, and show how to leverage public R&D to drive long-term corporate growth rather than a one-off product launch.

events.t: Access to Capital: Finding the Right Funding for Your Business
events.d:
From microloans and traditional lending to grants and crowdfunding, there’s no one-size-fits-all path to funding a business. Hear from local capital providers and entrepreneurs about the options available, how to determine which is right for you, and what it takes to successfully access the capital you need to start or grow.

Sponsored By ECDI

events.t: Imposter Freedom
events.d: An experiential, narrative-driven session that uses the untold story of the Wright brothers overcoming their imposter syndrome. Attendees will experience a radical reframing of startup anxiety and build the internal psychological safety necessary to survive the ups and downs of building something new.

events.t: Hot Wings & Hard Truths: Stop Waiting for Permission
events.d: What is stopping you from building the thing you keep talking about? Join Cincinnati builders from life sciences, gaming, and software for an honest conversation about starting before you feel qualified, building where you are instead of chasing the coasts, and creating with the community and talent already here. The questions get harder as the wings get hotter.

events.t: Ideation to Validation Work Session
events.d: Building on the core frameworks of the speaker’s newly released book, this high-energy, 45-minute interactive workshop moves attendees from passive listening to active execution. Participants will break out into competitive teams to rapidly build a hardware business concept from scratch, navigating the critical steps required to move a physical product securely through the earliest Technology Readiness Levels. Teams will pressure-test their unit economics, map out their manufacturing viability, and define their target market under tight constraints. The session culminates in a fast-paced pitch competition where groups present to a business panel, voting on who built the most viable, market-ready hardware venture.

events.t: The Investor Room: A Live Pitch with QCA Ventures
events.d:
Go behind the curtain of a real investor pitch as a startup founder takes the hot seat with three QCA Ventures investors. Hear the pitch, the questions, and the candid investor conversation that follows.

Sponsored by Queen City Angels

events.t: Ask a Banker: Funding-Ready Business Breakouts
events.d:
Sit down with U.S. Bank advisors and fellow entrepreneurs for candid, small-group conversations about accessing capital, preparing your business for funding, and the questions you’ve always wanted to ask a banker.

Sponsored by US Bank

events.t: Sex, Shame & Success: The Hidden Path to Creativity, Connection & Impact
events.d:
This session offers a deeply personal, experiential learning environment designed to spark curiosity and realization about intrapersonal expression and interpersonal growth. The talk will guide attendees through a safe exploration of how shame, pleasure, and an expanded understanding of consent dictate our personal and professional alignment.

Our sexuality lives at the absolute heart of play, curiosity, and creativity. It directly intersects with how we relate to security, power, and money. When we experience ecosystemic stress, we often resort to "splitting"—compartmentalizing our lives, suppressing our bodies, and severing our relational depth. This disconnection is the true root of creative blocks, organizational distress, and founder burnout.

events.t: Tackling Term Sheets : A Working Lunch with Thompson Hines
events.d:
Raising capital? Understanding term sheets is critical. Over lunch, Thompson Hine experts will break down key terms, common pitfalls, and negotiation tips to help founders protect their vision while building strong investor relationships. Connect with peers and get practical insights to navigate your next deal with confidence.

Sponsored by Thompson Hine

events.t: Build your first AI agent, no technical skills required.
events.d:
AI is moving quickly, but for many teams, it still feels abstract. Notion AI Labs is a hands-on workshop designed to turn AI ideas into workflows your team can actually use.

Join us for a guided workshop where you’ll learn how agents work and how to connect them to the workflows already happening in your workspace. You’ll walk away with an agent that you can immediately put to work. No Notion experience or technical skills required.

Sponsored By Notion

events.t: Women in Entrepreneurship: Real Talk Lunchpad
events.d: Meet other women business owners for lunch in a welcoming, supportive environment. You'll get and give business advice and feedback in small groups.

events.t: Building Businesses with Cincinnati Children's
events.d:
Most people assume that if you want to build a company around breakthrough medical science, you need to be the scientist. Cincinnati Children’s is proving otherwise. Our tech transfer and innovation team is actively building newcos and we are recruiting experienced operators to run them. In this session, our VP of Innovation Ventures and a panel of Cincinnati Children’s Entrepreneurs in Residence (EIRs) will pull back the curtain on how this model actually works: how assets get identified and de-risked, what a newco looks like before a CEO is even in the room, what we look for in the executives we recruit, and how the relationship between CEO and inventor is structured for the long haul. There will be time for Q&A.

Sponsored By Cincinnati Children's

events.t: The Automated Client Journey: How to Build a Business That Runs While You're Not Watching
events.d: Most founders hit a growth ceiling not because they need more people, but because they never built the systems that should have come first. This session walks through the five automations that create an invisible team — handling your client journey from first touch to loyal fan, without adding headcount. You'll leave with a clear picture of where your business is leaking revenue and exactly what to build to stop it.

events.t: Still Your Voice - Human Leadership In The Age of AI
events.d: This session is for high-achievers who are building, leading, and navigating complex environments in a world that keeps accelerating. It's not about whether to use AI. It's about ensuring that as AI expands what's possible, you remain the author of your choices. Drawing on the VOICCE® decision-making framework, speaker Tian Philson will walk participants through the leadership skill that no algorithm can replicate - the ability to slow down, get clear, and make aligned decisions in moments that matter most.

events.t: Resilience Requires Creativity: Why the Organizations Built to Survive Uncertainty Aren't Necessarily the Ones Built for Efficiency
events.d:
Today's businesses face volatility, uncertainty, complexity, and ambiguity at a scale few organizations were designed to handle. Yet when uncertainty rises, our instinct is often to seek more control: optimize processes, reduce risk, eliminate waste, and make outcomes increasingly predictable. That instinct may be making organizations more fragile.

Drawing from ongoing graduate research at Parsons School of Design, two decades of creative leadership, and conversations with leaders across design, innovation, and business, Christopher A. Ritter explores creativity as more than a source of ideas. It is an organizational capacity for adaptation.

This talk examines why resilient organizations protect curiosity, experimentation, candor, judgment, and the freedom to explore what isn't yet known—and why the ability to create may ultimately matter more than the ability to predict.

events.t: Ditch the Script: A Sales Approach That Actually Fits You
events.d: You're not bad at sales. You've just been handed someone else's script. Sales isn't a trick or a transaction. It's the beginning of an intimate relationship with your client, and that relationship starts at first contact. The problem is most sales training teaches you to follow a process designed for someone else entirely, and when it doesn't feel right, you assume something is wrong with you. Nothing is wrong with you. You just haven't been shown how YOU naturally build trust. In this session, you'll discover what makes you tick as a relationship builder, and use that to identify the lead generation approaches that fit how you're naturally wired. Through a quick assessment and guided group conversation, you'll walk away with a clear picture of how you're wired to connect, and a personalized short list of lead generation strategies that fit you, ready to use the next day.

events.t: Nobody Moves a Biotech Startup to Kentucky... Until They Do
events.d:
Led by Project MedTech, this discussion explores why a growing number of life sciences founders are choosing Cincinnati and Northern Kentucky to launch, relocate, and scale their companies.

While biotech is often associated with Boston, San Diego, and the Bay Area, innovative companies are increasingly finding advantages in emerging ecosystems that offer access to talent, infrastructure, strategic partnerships, and a collaborative startup community. Through a conversation with leaders from LifeSciKY, CARTx Therapeutics, and Clareo Biosciences, attendees will hear firsthand how founders evaluate where to build their companies, the challenges they face, and what resources have been critical to their success.

This session will provide founders, investors, students, and ecosystem builders with a candid look at the realities of building a high-growth life sciences startup in the Midwest and why the region is becoming a destination for innovation.

events.t: Anyone Can Code: Use AI to Make Your First $100,000
events.d: This will be a hands-on workshop where participants break into small groups and build their first AI agents for their businesses. Kameron Seabrook, tech founder of Obai, will guide participants through the process of thinking and building like a tech founder. Participants will learn the frameworks, tools, and mindset it takes to build great products. They’ll leave with a better understanding of how to: Turn an idea into a working product using AI Build and prototype without needing to be an experienced developer Protect their intellectual property and inventions Think through ways to sell and monetize what they’ve built It will be a jam-packed, hands-on 40-minute session.

events.t: Magnetic Communication: The Guide to Confidence On & Off Stage
events.d: This high-impact workshop is focused on helping entrepreneurs become more confident, compelling communicators, preparing them for pitching investors, speaking on panels, networking, creating content, or leading teams. Inspired by the practical storytelling techniques of Vinh Giang, the persuasive communication strategies of Codie Sanchez, and the behavioral science insights of Vanessa Van Edwards, this session teaches attendees how to command attention, speak with clarity and confidence, use body language intentionally, and communicate in a way that builds trust and influence. The workshop is interactive, actionable, and designed specifically for founders who want to elevate both their personal brand and business opportunities through stronger communication skills.

events.t: Know Your Numbers: Financial Clarity for Confident Small Business Decisions
events.d: Many entrepreneurs are passionate about their work but feel overwhelmed or disconnected from their business finances. This panel will explore how financial clarity helps small business owners make stronger decisions around pricing, cash flow, taxes, and sustainable growth. Attendees will hear practical insights on common money mistakes, early financial warning signs, and how to use their numbers as a leadership tool rather than something they only look at during tax season.

events.t: Lab to License: A Live Negotiation
events.d: Individuals representing a university's TTO and a spinout negotiate a fictional license agreement in real time (including equity, royalties, milestones, sub-licensing rights, and milestone expectations) giving the audience an inside look at the strategy, tension, and tradeoffs behind university innovation deals. The session runs two scenarios, one pharma and one digital health.

events.t: Making Technology More Human
events.d: The future of technology is not about replacing people. It is about empowering them. In a world increasingly focused on automation and artificial intelligence, this session challenges founders and innovators to rethink how products are designed, built, and adopted. Attendees will explore how human-centered technology can reduce friction, strengthen decision-making, and help people do their best work without sacrificing the human element that drives innovation, trust, and lasting impact.

events.t: Mission to Measurement: A Simple Framework for Making Smarter Business Decisions
events.d: Most small businesses don’t struggle because of a lack of data. They struggle because their data is fragmented, unclear, or disconnected from decision-making. In this workshop, attendees will learn a practical framework for aligning business goals, metrics, and operating rhythms so they can move from reactive decision-making to confident action. Drawing from enterprise analytics experience adapted for founder-led businesses, this session will provide approachable, actionable guidance without unnecessary complexity.

events.t: Employee Engagement as a Profitability Strategy
events.d:
Understanding how to engage and motivate your people is not a luxury program reserved for Fortune 500 companies – it’s a critical business driver that makes or breaks small to medium sized businesses. We’ll review the link between leadership style, employee motivation and performance, along with insights to positively impact to your bottom line.

Sponsored by Insperity

events.t: Build the Business You Actually Want: An Operating Model for Bootstrapped Entrepreneurs
events.d: Not every entrepreneur wants or needs to build a scalable startup, and that is not a lesser path. In this session, attendees will explore how side-hustle entrepreneurs, solo operators, and bootstrapped growth-company builders can use the Entrepreneur, Manager, and Technician roles to choose the business model they actually want. Through practical examples and a live AI-assisted workflow demonstration, attendees will learn how to systematize repeatable work, improve consistency, and create more room to work on the business instead of only in it.

events.t: Growing Our Region Through Bold Bets
events.d:
What happens when a region stops thinking organization by organization—and starts making bigger bets together? Cincinnati’s next chapter of growth will require more than any one company, institution, or initiative. It will take a connected region willing to align around ambitious ideas, combine our strengths, and take bold swings on what’s possible.

To close out StartupCincy Week, regional leaders come together for a forward-looking conversation about the big bets being placed across Cincinnati—from economic development and talent to tourism, placemaking, entrepreneurship, and innovation. We’ll explore where momentum is building, where greater collaboration can unlock new opportunities, and how a more connected region creates the conditions for founders, innovators, and growing companies to thrive. Because when Cincinnati bets boldly on itself, we give the people building what’s next even more reason to build it here.

events.t: StartupCincy 10 Year Anniversary Party! Presented by VisitCincy
events.d: Celebrate 10 years of StartupCincy with the people who built it—and the community carrying it forward. Join us at The Transept for a bigger-than-usual anniversary party featuring music, heavy apps, drinks, and a few familiar faces from across a decade of Cincinnati’s startup ecosystem. Presented by VisitCincy.

events.t: SUCW Student Day Kickoff!
events.d:
Union Hall - Beer Hall

Join us as we kick off the sweetest day of the week! Chase Dawson and Alex Yocum of Swirley's Soft Serve will dive deep into a discussion about entrepreneurship, the ecosystem that has supported them, and the importance of University led resources.

events.t: The Money Behind the Startups: A Venture Capital Primer
events.d: Venture capital is one of the most talked-about and least understood corners of finance. In this hour-long session, Cintrifuse Capital's Ilana Habib pulls back the curtain on how VC actually works — where it came from, how it operates today, and where it's headed. You'll learn the incentives that drive both investors and founders, why the industry behaves the way it does, and how to navigate a landscape that's shifting fast. Built for aspiring founders and investors alike, this is a candid, inside look at the deals and dynamics behind the checks

events.t: Founder Tools
events.d:
Are you a student founder looking to make your business more efficient with AI? Or just curious about the hottest new AI tools out there? Either way, this is the session for you.

You'll hear from Rahul, Expert in Residence at Cintrifuse Capital, breaking down the AI tools reshaping sales, finance, go-to-market, and more. He'll share what's actually working right now, so you can walk away with tools you can apply immediately.

Whether you're trying to save time, cut costs, or scale smarter, this session will help you take your startup to the next level.

events.t: Startup Fellows Lounge
events.d: Curious about becoming a Startup Fellow? Stop by the Startup Fellows Lounge anytime Thursday to meet Fellows alumni, the Cintrifuse Capital team, and the program’s future coordinator. Get your questions answered, hear what the experience is really like, drop your resume, and get a head start on making connections with the team behind the next Startup Fellows cohort.

events.t: The Two-Loop Founder: How Lean Teams Build and Sell at the Same Time
events.d: How do you quickly go from an idea to something customers will actually pay for without a huge team? Adam Tucker and Jake Smierciak A team of two will walk you through how to move from problem to product to customer. Come ready to rethink what you can build and how quickly you can get it out the door.

events.t: Build your first AI agent, no technical skills required.
events.d:
AI is moving quickly, but for many teams, it still feels abstract. Notion AI Labs is a hands-on workshop designed to turn AI ideas into workflows your team can actually use.

Join us for a guided workshop where you’ll learn how agents work and how to connect them to the workflows already happening in your workspace. You’ll walk away with an agent that you can immediately put to work. No Notion experience or technical skills required.

Sponsored By Notion

events.t: Startup Internships Demystified: Real Talk from Students and Educators
events.d: Join students and educators from regional universities for a candid conversation about startup internships across Greater Cincinnati/NKY. The panel will explore how students find and succeed in startup roles, what makes these experiences different from traditional internships, and how campuses can better connect emerging talent with startup opportunities. Attendees will leave with practical insights on pathways, expectations, and next steps for getting involved in the startup ecosystem.

events.t: The Next Wave of Venture
events.d: A new generation of investors are joining the venture capital landscape and shaping what’s next. Join us as these student-led funds break down how venture capital works, what investors look for and the role student-led funds play in building the next generation of investors and entrepreneurs.

events.t: Student Day Community Lunch!
events.d: Take a break, grab a bite, and connect with the StartupCincy community! Join fellow students, founders, mentors, and ecosystem leaders for a casual community lunch on the final day of StartupCincy Week. Boxed lunches will be available first come, first served, so come early, grab a seat, and make a few new connections.

events.t: Make Yourself Impossible Not to Hire
events.d: How to turn an internship into a full-time role

events.t: Get Unstuck: Speed Coaching for Startup Students
events.d:

Sarah Rodriguez: Homespun
events.d:
An archive of tangible memories

Artist Sarah Rodriguez’s work is an archive of tangible memories. Analyzing concepts of kinship and womanhood through discarded objects. Once reclaimed, objects are adorned and preserved, reflecting the intricacies of our lives, suspended between times of joy and sorrow.

With an emphasis on tactility, the work incorporates a variety of materials and techniques. Glitter, yarn, buttons, and beads are carefully assembled, forming text and highlighting the functionality of the object. Together, these elements examine the duality between the playfulness of girlhood and the weight and labor womanhood bears.

This practice seeks to honor the ordinary, transforming familiar materials into talismans of memory. By inviting viewers into this tactile archive, Rodriguez creates space for reflection on the stories we inherit, the ones we carry, and the ones we choose to preserve.

events.t: SOFTlab: Gravity's Rainbow
events.d:
A floating symphony of color and form

This installation, suspended from the ceiling of the CAC’s Dr. Stanley & Mickey Kaplan Hall Lobby, takes something invisible—gravity—and makes it visible. New York-based design firm SOFTlab constructed a frame made from shapes that mimic clustering bubbles. The custom cut and printed paper strips draped from this structure drift slowly up and down, following the movements of computer-controlled winches, causing their arcing forms to adapt to gravity’s pull. The hues of the brightly colored paper strips intermix as they adjust to the rise and fall of the winch, creating constantly changing patterns and colors. Taken together, these simple shapes generate a complex symphony of color and form.

SOFTlab found inspiration for this work in the floating concrete volumes of the Zaha Hadid-designed Lois & Richard Rosenthal Center for Contemporary Art. Stacked above Kaplan Hall’s open space, the forms appear to be floating, yet their heavy materials create a sense of stability. SOFTlab’s sculptural installation hangs from these boxes into the CAC’s voluminous, light-filled lobby, working with Hadid’s design to amplify the building’s own sense of gravity.

events.t: Yayoi Kusama: All the Eternal Love I Have for the Pumpkins
events.d:
Yayoi Kusama: All the Eternal Love I Have for the Pumpkins (2016) features an array of yellow gourds of various sizes, adorned with black polka dots, that are surrounded by mirrors. The result is an immersive installation that allows the visitor to become part of the artwork as they seemingly enter an infinite field of glowing pumpkins.

All the Eternal Love I Have for the Pumpkins illustrates Kusama’s characteristic themes, including infinity and obsessive repetition. The artist has described the pumpkin—one of her quintessential symbols—as a form of self-portraiture. A rare assemblage of a dozen Pumpkin acrylic paintings on canvas made between 1990-2004 will also greet gallery visitors, courtesy of the Masterworks Foundation.

Kusama’s career spans more than seven decades, and her Infinity Mirror Rooms are some of her most experimental and iconic works, often incorporating a variety of illuminated objects.

Infinity Mirror Room—Phalli’s Field (1965) was Kusama’s first installation to use mirrors to create a sense of endless space, featuring a floor covered in hundreds of red-spotted, white fabric-stuffed tubes. Kusama’s mirrored installations represented an innovative step in the emergence of an increasingly experiential practice. In each work, the visitor’s reflection seems to extend into infinity while they simultaneously have an intimate and individualized room experience.

All the Eternal Love I Have for the Pumpkins draws on Kusama’s seminal pumpkin room, Mirror Room (Pumpkin) (1991), which was shown at for the Japanese Pavilion at the 1993 Biennale Arte in Venice.

Yayoi Kusama: All the Eternal Love I Have for the Pumpkins is on loan from the Dallas Museum of Art.

events.t: Entre Lo Que Fue y Lo Que Es (Between What Was and What Is)
events.d:
Works by artist collaborative Batres Gilvin.

Works by Batres Gilvin reflect a meditation on in-between states, where memory, identity, and the body shift between presence and absence.

Batres Gilvin, an artist collaborative in Greater Cincinnati, is comprised of Karla Batres and Bradly Gilvin, life partners who met in 2011 while studying at the Art Academy of Cincinnati. In a multiethnic partnership that joins the personal with the professional, Batres’ Mexican American heritage and Gilvin’s Southern American roots are a catalyst for complicated conversations about difference, otherness, and identity. In their Morning View, Kentucky studio located on the property of the Gilvin family farm and homestead, Batres Gilvin explores the local and global implications of immigration. Their artistic work is informed as much by larger political conversations as it is by life on the farm and daily interactions with Bradly and Karla’s immediate and extended family.

In Batres Gilvin’s artistic work art becomes life and vice versa. As a multiethnic collaborative, Batres Gilvin is a study in contradictions. Playful irreverence exists alongside unflinching solemnity. An unsparing commentary on the inequities of US immigration policy is wrapped in sparkly, kitschy imagery, providing a sugar-coated dose of truth serum, Mexican American style. In Batres Gilvin’s world, contradiction is both material and tool; it is also a reminder of the complexity of humans and the necessity of holding space for difficult conversations.

events.t: Unfolding Elegance: European Fans from the Taft Collection
events.d: Featuring sumptuous decoration and beautifully detailed paintings, the nine 18th-century fans in Unfolding Elegance represent the pinnacle of fan-making in Europe and a level of craftsmanship that was unrivaled in later periods. The museum’s rare examples depict classical myths, pastoral scenes, and biblical stories—images only seen when a woman unfurled and delicately fluttered her fan. In preparation for the exhibition, a conservator is spending over a year stabilizing these fragile objects, making it possible to share them with the public after years of being held in storage.

There is no single place to experience the performances—and that’s the point—wander, climb, pause, listen, and discover how the music shifts as you move between plazas. You are invited to join the performance with musical instruments, which you can make at the CAM Cruiser before the music starts, or percussion instruments that will be provided. From 3–5 p.m. we invite you to create a Community Canvas with Happen Inc., celebrating the fall season. The five plazas will continue to host our thematic visual interpretations, creating a perfect end-of-day photo op for guests.

1 p.m. Five-minute meditation with The Well
1–2 p.m. Instrument making with the CAM Cruiser and collaborative set building

events.t: Indigenous Peoples’ Day Convergence exhibition
events.d:
An Urban Native Collective Exhibition

Urban Native Collective is a Cincinnati-based organization that serves the broad interests and needs of the Indigenous community within the Tri-State area. Urban Native Collective presents its eighth Indigenous People’s Day Convergence. This four-day celebration, which includes this exhibition, focuses on current issues affecting the Indigenous community, their past, their resilience and their bright future.

The Indigenous Peoples’ Day Convergence exhibition is presented in partnership with the Contemporary Arts Center in The Collective Gallery sponsored by P&G, located in the lower lobby. It brings together contemporary artists to highlight that Indigenous expression is not a recover of what was lost, but an explosive celebration of what has always survived. Moving beyond colonial narratives, the exhibition honors Indigenous life as a living, Sovereign, and evolving force. Grounded in an “Indigenized” punk aesthetic, this multidisciplinary showcase demonstrates that Indigenous presence, creative defiance, and joy are the ultimate forces shaping our shared future.

Artists presented in this exhibition include Jaque Fragua "Mobil Savage" (Pueblo), Robert Franklin (Diné), Steph Littlebird (Grand Ronde), Kobi Morgan (Diné), Cole Reuben (Seneca), Sara Siestreem (Hanis Coos), Mariana Varela (Mexican), Hiro Cash (Diné), Jeremy Dennis (Shinnicok), Carlos Ramirez (Mexican), Isaiah Stewart (Oglala Lakota / Mohawk) and Solstar (Mayan). Curated by Leonard D. Harmon (Nanticoke).

The opening reception for this exhibition will be on Friday, October 9th, from 5 to 9 p.m. It will feature performances from the Copper Face United Powwow Troupe and DJ Creepingbear. Tortilleria Garcia will have a selection of food items for purchase. The reception and performance are free and open to the public.

events.t: Leonard Harmon - People of the Good River
events.d:
Challenging misconceptions of Indigenous culture

Indigenous culture is too often trapped in history books or reduced to outdated stereotypes. People of the Good River challenges these misconceptions by capturing the vibrant, everyday realities of Indigenous people living in Cincinnati today. Grounded in the legacy of the Ohi-yo—the Seneca word for "Good River"—this exhibition pairs candid portrait photography with hand-pulled screen printing on paper. Each physical layer of ink builds a portrait of modern life, work, and community, moving past romanticized tropes to celebrate an enduring present and archive for the people who are actively shaping Cincinnati's contemporary narrative.

“They say the truth is in the eye of the beholder… but who’s looking?” ~ Leonard Harmon

Leonard Harmon has always been drawn to a life of expression. Leonard credits a large part of his passion too. As he puts it, his “direct bloodline to art”. His father was a furniture maker, and his uncle, and namesake Leonard Allen Harmon, was a well-known portrait artist featured in the Heard Museum of Arizona. Art, in one form or the other, was always present in his life. As a young man, he was inspired by his grandparents' love of cooking to attend Johnson & Wales University, one of the finest culinary schools in the country, where he not only learned the fine art of creating culinary masterpieces but also began to explore his love of music. Eventually touring the country as a DJ, it wasn’t until 2010 that Leonard began to explore a new form of expression, traditional and contemporary mixed media.

In an interview with The Stranger, Leonard explains, “I like using older images to tell a new story of putting perspective on our history. As a new artist, I like exploring all kinds of methods and mediums. Each new style I incorporate helps me express myself in a new way. I’m never scared to try new things and see where my mind takes me.”

A citizen of the Lenape Tribe of New Jersey and the Nanticoke Tribe of Delaware, Leonard currently lives on the Confederated Tribes of Siletz Indian Reservation. He reflects often on traveling to Connecticut and Oklahoma to attend Powwows and be immersed in his culture. He continues to be actively involved in tribal traditions on the Siletz Reservation. This immersion is seen in his work as he takes inspiration from his ancestors to put modern spins on traditional arts.

Curated by CAC's Education Department

Grounded in an "Indigenized" punk aesthetic, this multidisciplinary showcase demonstrates that Indigenous presence, creative defiance, and joy are the ultimate forces shaping our shared future.

events.t: “Equal to Any in the City:” Ball & Thomas Photographs, 1840s–1870s
events.d: “Equal to Any in the City:” Ball & Thomas Photographs, 1840s–1870s reveals the pioneering work of photographers James Presley Ball and Alexander S. Thomas, whose studios helped shape early photographic culture in 19th-century Cincinnati. Drawing on the Cincinnati Museum Center’s rich collection of their work (the largest known), the exhibition examines Ball’s training, his decision to establish a studio in Cincinnati, and the collaborative role of his family and professional partners in producing and circulating photographic images. Through portraits, studio scenes, and contextual materials, the exhibition reveals how photography functioned as both an artistic and social medium in the mid-19th century. Visitors are invited to learn how photographs were produced, experience sitting for a portrait, and discover the technologies, props, and retouching techniques that defined early studio photography. The exhibition also highlights Ball’s connections to Cincinnati’s vibrant Black community and abolitionist networks, demonstrating how photography intersected with social reform movements and the cultural life of the city during a pivotal era in American history.

events.t: Getting Technical: Alternative Photographic Processes
events.d: Spanning approximately 175 years, Getting Technical navigates the varying and conflicting definitions of “alternative processes.” The exhibition features historical practices prior to the invention of gelatin silver prints, some of which lack factory-ready materials, produce images with a lensless camera, or require hand-manipulation. Photography was born out of interest in science and chemistry, dedication to trial-and-error, and the circulation of ideas and enthusiasm amongst photographers. This exhibition honors those early commitments to experimentation and their lasting influence.

events.t: Alexander Liberman: The Artist in His Studio
events.d:
The Artist in His Studio presents photographs by Alexander Liberman that document some of the most influential multidisciplinary artists of the 20th century within the spaces where they lived and worked. Created over more than a decade, Liberman’s photographs capture painters and sculptors of the School of Paris—including figures such as Pablo Picasso, Georges Braque, Marc Chagall, Henri Matisse, and Alberto Giacometti—surrounded by their tools, materials, and unfinished works. Unlike traditional portraiture, these images reveal the intimate environments of artistic production and the personalities behind modern art. At the same time, the exhibition highlights the remarkable range of Liberman’s own creative life.

Born in Kyiv, Ukraine, and later emigrating to the United States, Liberman built an influential career as a photographer, painter, sculptor, and longtime art director at Vogue. His photographs reflect the perspective of an artist documenting fellow artists—what one curator described as “a Vasari with a camera.” The exhibition also resonates with Pyramid Hill’s permanent collection, which includes several of Liberman’s monumental steel sculptures installed throughout the landscape. Together, these photographs and sculptures reveal Liberman’s lifelong engagement with form, scale, and artistic community across media.
